# 233 Developers Discussed Abandoning the Office Add-in Platform — An Open Letter on the Office.js Stability, Security & Trust Crisis

## An Open Letter from the Office Add-in Developer Community

**To:** Microsoft Office Extensibility Team, Microsoft 365 Platform Team, Microsoft Developer Relations  
**From:** The Office Add-in Developer Community  
**Date:** February 2026  
**Subject:** Critical Platform Stability, Security & Trust Issues Requiring Immediate Action

---

## Executive Summary

We are writing to formally raise our deep concerns about the **stability, reliability, security, and long-term viability** of the Office.js add-in platform.

This letter is informed by a comprehensive analysis of **every issue filed in the OfficeDev/office-js GitHub repository** — over **6,200 issues** spanning 7+ years. results.title: [Feature Request] Space for triage notes on alert preview modal
results.body_snippet:
### Problem Description
When triaging alerts, there is no space to record an explanation for the triage outcome.  These notes are valuable when one team member is triaging alerts and assigning cases to other team members.  In cases where alerts are not converted to cases, the notes are valuable during regular reviews to make sure nothing was missed.  

These are some thoughts on how to handle the alert triage notes for various triage outcome scenarios:

1. **Further investigation of the alert is warranted / Alert is used to create a case-**
  Triage notes should be preserved in the alert "preview" modal and displayed in the case somewhere.  My preference would be for the notes from each alert to be add to a 'Review alert notes' task.  If there is more than one alert added to a case, the notes from each alert can be added to the 'Review alert notes' task as a new task log. 
2. **The alert warrants no actions or investigation-**
  Triage notes should be preserved in the alert "preview" modal for review/audit purposes.  
3. **The thing generating the alert requires fixing-**
  Triage notes should be preserved in the alert "preview" modal for review.

results.body_snippet:
# Proposal: Add Attack Type Classification to Malware Advisories

## Problem Statement

The current malware advisory system in the GitHub Advisory Database creates a significant security coverage gap. **Dependabot suppresses all malware advisories** due to high false positive rates from substitution attacks, but this blanket suppression also prevents alerts for critical threats like legitimate maintainer account compromises.

### Recent Critical Incidents Missed by Dependabot

**September 8-9, 2025**: The qix account compromise affected 18+ popular packages (chalk, debug, ansi-styles) with 2+ billion weekly downloads. Malware was designed to steal cryptocurrency by intercepting wallet transactions.
- Advisory: GHSA-8mgj-vmr8-frr6 (debug), GHSA-ch7m-m9rf-8gvv (color-convert), etc.
- **Result**: Dependabot users received NO alerts despite critical compromise

**August 26, 2025**: The nx package compromise affected 3.5M+ weekly downloads, harvesting credentials, GitHub tokens, and cryptocurrency wallets from developer machines.
- Advisory: GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c
- **Result**: Dependabot users received NO alerts despite supply chain injection

### Current Advisory Quality Issues

results.title: George's knowledge share for Alertmanager maintainers
results.body_snippet:
# Background

This issue contains all the Alertmanager naunces that I've learned over the years and changes I have been thinking about to try and fix some of the problems I have found (sadly I have found many). It is about time I wrote it up to help future maintainers make informed decisions for the project and understand where there be dragons 🐉.

# Gotchas

The following is a list of "gotchas" that I have found while contributing to Alertmanager:

## GroupKey is supposed to be unique but it is not

The GroupKey is a key derived from the matchers in the route (including any parent routes) and any labels in the `group_by` field of the matching route.

There are a number of cases where GroupKey is not unique such that it is possible for two or more aggregation groups to share the same GroupKey at the same time.

This creates a number of problems:

1. If the receiver is also the same, two or more aggregation groups can share the same notification log.
2. If we want to use GroupKey in the "GroupMarker" then two aggregation groups with conflicted GroupKeys will overwrite each other's markers.

A simple solution to this problem is to add names for routes, and each name must be unique at

We urgently request the return of **Native Push Notifications** for Glide Apps. results.title: Audio Feedback for Task Status 🔉
results.body_snippet:
### Feature Description

You should add audio feedback for task completion and replies. 
This will give users an immediate audible alert when a task finishes or when you respond. Your current notification settings already allow banner and sound alerts for task completion, waiting for action, and abnormal stop events. Each status has its own sound file and a play option. The volume control is set to maximum, which ensures alerts are heard clearly.

Extend this setup to include a sound for successful task completion and for replies. Use short, distinct audio clips so users can identify the status without looking at the screen. This will improve response time and help users act quickly when a task changes state.

### Use Case

You enable audio feedback for task completion and reply. When a task finishes, you hear a short sound that confirms success. When a reply is ready, you hear a different sound. You set distinct audio files for each status so you can identify them instantly. You keep the volume high to ensure alerts are audible even when you are away from the screen. This helps you respond faster, reduces missed updates, and keeps your workflow moving without constant visual check

results.title: [Security Solution] Failed detection rule execution to increment additional look-back of next execution
results.body_snippet:
**Describe the feature:**

Currently if a rule does not run on schedule then the Detection Engine will automatically attempt to cover time that was missed the next time the rule does run. However, failures during a rule execution will not cause the next rule execution to re-search that older window.

**Describe a specific use case for the feature:**

If rule execution does not run because of elasticsearch exception, next execution should use additional look-back time incremented to look at time since last successful execution
A common cause of rule execution failure is `no_shard_available_action_exception` which is more common to take place on elasticsearch cluster whereby creating index takes longer because any index is first created in red health till primary shards become active... A search on data stream when one index is red because execution run just instant after data stream rolled over will cause detection rule execution to fail.
If a rule runs every 5 minutes with 1 minute additional look-back - a single execution failure will cause a blind spot of 4 minutes... If the look-back was set to 6 minutes on next execution then no data will be missed

results.body_snippet:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We would love to use robusta in our production environment as part of our alerting mechanism. our use case would be to use robusta to kill a pod on the back of an alert. This would save the on call engineer having to receive a pager and manually perform this. However, as the runner/forwarder aren't scalable without duplicate notification we can't utilise this tool in production due to availability concerns.

 We would like the runner/forwarder pods to be able to scale horizontally to ensure alerts aren't missed and runbook are actioned.

results.title: Remote Management for Duplicati
results.body_snippet:
I would like to see Remote Management for Duplicati.  Perhaps something like:

-Duplicati installed with a commandline switch for management server (or in the GUI)
-Duplicati generates a unique key and registers with the management server (with it's computer name/domain/workgroup) and awaits instructions
-Server admin approves new Duplicati client and assigns it a template (what to backup and where) as well as credentials for the backup repo and encryption key
-Server ensures that the client keeps to schedule and if there are deviations or backup errors, it's reported to the admin
-Server should be written to work on a standard LAMP stack for deployment to commodity hosting if at all possible, and have security in mind.  Cronjob to run compliance failure alerts (missed backups or clients not checking in, etc.)
-Nice to have: restore files from the management console to the client, or to be downloaded directly from the console

Kenneth mentioned he had much of this already written, he may be able to make available his progress.

Google Cloud, specifically GKE, can notify of lifecycle events:
- security issue
- upcoming forced upgrade
- end of support notification

They do this via pubsub, https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-notifications has some information

We would like to harmonise this with keep since it is adjacent to the current alerts around CVE in containers and runtime errors.

I believe a generic PubSub provider would be quite similar to webhook/json based ones. A topic, a filter, and then messages would flow. Each message would have a object-payload that could be extracted and create an alert.
